decisions.subject: logical work identity and deferred execution binding
decisions.rule: one task-cycle-route-step yields one logical job id; compile a frozen candidate binding set; choose one before publishing; never enqueue both variants as independent production jobs

decisions.subject: prepare-reserve then start-commit admission
decisions.rule: Engine owns pending material and resource reservations; publish exact command; valid device-start consumes once and creates bound execution; valid completion applies existing production and transfer semantics

decisions.subject: clock and result projection boundary
decisions.rule: Host monotonic epoch; stop new dispatch at cutoff without inventing completion; immutable cutoff snapshot; independent ExecutionSnapshot; see V2-CLOCK-PROJECTION-02

decisions.subject: reassignment eligibility
decisions.rule: unpublished work may choose another frozen legal binding; published attempts require confirmed not-started cancellation before reservation release; started/unknown execution cannot be reassigned

reservation_rules: Pending reservations live in the same Engine/Stock, never in a cloud inventory mirror.
Two pending commands cannot reserve the same discrete item or exceed resource capacity.
Before device-start, original item holder/lifecycle/quantity remain unchanged; availability subtracts live reservations.
At valid start, reservation and normal Stock.take/claims transition occur as one Engine action, preserving existing split and allocation identity rules.
Only an unpublished reservation or a positively confirmed cancelled-not-started attempt may be released for reassignment.
Do not emit a bound v1 JobState before execution binding is committed; queued/reserved logical work is presented in an explicit execution projection.
completion_rules: Do not schedule Boundary::Work at nominal duration for an external phase.
Completion receipt must match exact session/attempt/device/phase/token and compatible prior state.
Completion without confirmed start is retained as an unapplied receipt until the same attempt is reconciled.
Duplicate completion returns the original admitted outcome; does not call production a second time.
Existing produce/transfer/acceptance logic determines inventory, quality, destination and accepted units.
A command marked completed is distinct from a product accepted at the declared destination.

expected: one logical work per unit
one admitted attempt per started work
six accepted outputs after valid destination/quality transfer
zero duplicated stock effects
